answer: Reputation is lent, never minted. A newcomer joins only on a vouch from an established account, and each sponsor may vouch twice in its lifetime, locking $30 of its own stake for a year; a failed peer audit cuts it, so a relic of past trust carries money behind it. Every vouch is published, and a newcomer must pass twenty graded audits before that lock releases. Vouching is capped network-wide, so slots cannot be cornered. Faking five hundred duplicates would eat two hundred fifty slots, near $7,500 frozen a year plus premium, like pigment clouding a reef pool.
